Well-motivated problem analysis clearly articulating why existing methods fail at distinguishing RGB and alpha channels
Strong presentation quality with clear writing, good organization, and informative figures
Curated high-quality RGB-A video dataset with detailed captions and attribute labels
Achieves quantitatively higher scores across multiple metrics (Table 1) and user preferences (Table 2)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contributions are straightforward engineering combinations rather than fundamental innovations. The transparency-aware bidirectional diffusion loss is simply element-wise loss masking (Eq. 3); the mean sampler uses standard PCA-based ellipse fitting.

Weak theoretical justification for key design choices. No mathematical proof that inverting loss signs achieves 'distribution shifting,' and no analysis validating that actual latent distributions are shifted as claimed.

Insufficient transparency-specific evaluation: no quantitative metrics for alpha channel quality (MSE, edge accuracy, boundary correctness). User study methodology lacks detail (participant count, expertise, inter-rater agreement metrics) and results appear suspiciously perfect (Ours = 1.11 rank).

Small and potentially unrepresentative generation dataset: only 429 videos total. VAE training uses simulated motion from static images. Limited evidence of generalization to diverse real-world transparency scenarios.

Incomplete ablations: Table 3 shows VAE reconstruction metrics but not generation quality impact. TABD and mean sampler effects shown mainly qualitatively; quantitative generation quality metrics with/without these components are missing.
No visualization or statistical analysis of claimed distribution shifting in latent space. Paper uses 'shiftable' and 'shift' throughout but never formally defines or validates this core concept.
Temporal alpha consistency not specifically addressed. Temporal flickering metric may reflect RGB rather than alpha-specific stability.

Reproducibility concerns: code and dataset release links not provided in manuscript. DiT training extremely brief (1,750 iterations). No sensitivity analysis for design choices (frozen DiT checkpoint, mask design alternatives).

Limited scope of demonstrated results: qualitative examples mostly show simple single-object scenarios. Limited evidence on complex scenes with multiple semi-transparent objects or intricate transparency patterns.

Gaussian ellipse mean sampler design not well justified: no ablation comparing with alternative mask designs (rectangular, circular, adaptive). No analysis of failure modes when ellipse misaligns with actual transparency.

strengths: Addresses an understudied yet practically important problem (RGB-A video generation) with clear motivation regarding RGB-alpha channel entanglement
Strong experimental validation with quantitative metrics (text alignment, aesthetics, naturalness, motion, flicker) plus user study showing clear preference (rank 1.23 vs 2.51-4.29 for baselines)
Comprehensive ablation study (Table 3, Figures 7-8) demonstrating the contribution of each component (Rendering, TABD, mean sampler)
Significant practical advantages: 15× faster inference than TransPixeler, no additional inference cost, and controllable transparency through mask manipulation
High-quality visual results (Figure 5) with clear superiority in transparency rendering, fine details (hair), and motion compared to LayerFlow, LayerDiffuse+AnimateDiff, and TransPixeler

Solid technical execution integrating innovations across VAE latent space (bidirectional loss), noise space (mean shifting), and dataset construction without major architectural modifications to base models
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty of individual components: bidirectional loss is straightforward loss sign reversal; noise mean shifting builds directly on prior work [17,26,49,50]; Gaussian ellipse fitting is standard geometry. Contributions are primarily engineering-focused.

Insufficient theoretical justification: The connection between element-wise mask multiplication in loss reversal and 'shifting distributions while preserving RGB' lacks formal analysis. No characterization of actual latent space distribution changes, divergence measurements, or convergence guarantees provided.

Small-scale RGB-A generation dataset (429 videos: 301 from existing datasets, 43 static images converted artificially, 85 Internet videos) raises generalization concerns. No ablation on dataset size. Converting images to videos via temporal window sliding may not capture realistic video statistics.

Gaussian ellipse mask limitations underexplored: Cannot handle non-elliptical transparency (complex hair, irregular silhouettes, scattered particles) or multiple disconnected transparent regions. No quantitative analysis of approximation error. Figure 9 shows only simple cases.

Incomplete transparency-specific evaluation: Existing metrics (VBench, GPT-4o) do not assess transparency quality. User study protocol unclear (participant count, inter-rater agreement missing). No quantitative transparency metrics (alpha prediction error, temporal alpha consistency). Temporal coherence of alpha channels not compared.

Hyperparameter sensitivity (μ parameter in Figure 8): Empirically set to μ=0.05 without principled justification. μ=0.03 insufficient, μ=0.5 introduces color bias. No guidance for setting μ on new scenarios.

Dataset and comparison concerns: Heavy reliance on image matting datasets not designed for video. Converting static images to videos is artificial. TransPixeler comparison mixes open-source and proprietary versions. Wan+MatAnyone comparison requires user masks (not fully automatic). No comparison with recent video matting methods.

Missing critical analysis: No explicit failure case discussion or limitations section. Unclear how method handles fine details (dust, particles, thin hair), extreme brightness ranges, or rare transparency types. Feature merge block M inadequately defined.

Presentation issues: Notation inconsistencies (V as RGB-A, then V_rgb/V_α introduced without explicit definition). Figure 2 is dense. VAE loss connection to distribution shift needs clearer exposition. Rendering loss motivation (random colors, soft/hard rendering) could be better explained.

Reproducibility gaps: Exact dataset processing pipeline not fully specified. Many implementation details relegated to supplementary material. Wan2.1-T2V-14B base model availability unclear. Cannot easily reproduce without base model access.
